claims.experiment: LTE rotational diagram of CH3CHO lines, with source size set to half a beam
claims.result: T_rot = 87±47 K and N = 2±1 x 10^15 cm^-2 (opacity < 0.4)
claims.finding: Hot corino with T ~100 K detected in HH212; first in Orion

evidence.quote: indicates temperature of 87$\pm$47 K and a column density of 2$\pm$1 $\times$ 10$^{15}$ cm$^{-2}$
We report the first detection of a hot corino in Orion.

claims.hypothesis: Is the low-velocity HDO asymmetry produced by the rotating disk or the infalling envelope?
claims.experiment: Comparison of HDO peak brightness and velocities with disk and envelope kinematics and spatial scales
claims.result: Disk origin would need a factor-2 non-axisymmetry; infall would give resolved peak emission
claims.finding: Disk and infall origins are disfavoured

evidence.quote: However, the low-velocity range of the HDO line being due to the protostellar disk is not supported
We can also rule out an origin from the rotating infalling envelope

claims.hypothesis: Is the low-velocity HDO emission dominated by outflowing gas?
claims.experiment: Optically thin LVG and kinematic arguments comparing HDO with SiO and SO outflow tracers
claims.result: HDO brightness in the red lobe; SO shows low-velocity compact bipolar outflow
claims.finding: Outflowing motions are the most likely origin of low-velocity HDO

evidence.quote: The last and most likely possibility is that the low-velocity HDO emission is dominated by outflowing motions.
Hence, it seems quite plausible that the low-velocity HDO would trace the inner region

claims.result: Source size 18–37 AU, T 70–110 K, n 1e9–1e10 cm^-3
claims.finding: Extremely small, dense, slowly outflowing emitting region

evidence.quote: The optically thick case thus also requires slow outflowing gas, further constraining the physical conditions

why_this_method.value: A non-LTE LVG model is used to compare the HDO signal with predictions, because the emission is unresolved and optical depth matters

evidence.quote: In order to understand the relative importance of each, we study two limit situations

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: HDO from the rotating protostellar disk: rejected on peak brightness and velocity asymmetry grounds

evidence.quote: First, the HDO emission might probe the rotating disk

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: HDO from the rotating infalling envelope: rejected because it would give spatially resolved peaks

evidence.quote: which would lead to spatially resolved peak emission, unlike the observed emission

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Optically thick infalling envelope (redshifted absorption): rejected in favour of blueshifted absorption from outflow

evidence.quote: because an optically thick infalling envelope would lead to redshifted absorption

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Small: one spectral-line ALMA dataset (two spectral windows of about 3.7 GHz each, 24 antennas, single epoch), likely a few GB of visibilities, inferred from the setup described.
reproducibility.score_reason: Data are an archival reuse of Codella et al. 2014 with public status not stated; imaging recipe and LVG inputs are largely missing, though line list, frequencies, beam and rms are given.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Public availability of the archival data is not stated in the paper, and key imaging and modelling settings are missing, so the recipe is not complete enough to redo the main results.
